correctness.rationale: The entire finite domain is exhausted. All 11,440 seven-subsets and 12,870 eight-subsets are checked by two independently implemented descendant encodings, which agree on every family. Exactly 240 seven-subsets pass and no eight-subset passes; heredity rules out all larger codes. The full 384-element Hamming-isometry group is then applied to all 240 maxima and yields exactly the claimed two orbits and stabilizers.

value.rationale: This is a natural finite boundary in a classical multimedia-fingerprinting code model: prior work supplies a seven-word construction while the quoted general upper bound is nine. Closing the binary length-four gap and classifying every equality case reveals two genuinely different extremal geometries, distinguished by their Hamming-distance distributions. The 240-code/two-orbit census is reusable as a benchmark for constructions and equivalence reductions, rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
